note: Run on NEAR testnet against Ref Finance pool 1084. For the slow-bleed run the owner tightened that key's leak budget to $0.06 (normally $0.20), so it trips in a few trades instead of a few dozen.

steps.title: An honest swap sets the reference price
steps.how: 0.3 wNEAR to USDT with a minimum 0.5% under the pool. The contract reads Ref's live quote before sending it and starts its own reference price from it.
steps.result: Executed. The contract checked the pool itself before sending the swap.

steps.title: A hacked guard signs a loose minimum
steps.how: A validly signed swap whose minimum output is 3% under what the pool pays right now. It is still above the owner's fixed price floor, so v5 would have let it through.
steps.result: The signed minimum output gives away 3.00% of what the pool pays right now. The limit is 1.00%.

steps.title: Slow bleed, trade 1: a 'fair-looking' give-away
steps.how: A $3.90 swap whose minimum is 0.9% under the pool. Under the 1% limit, so it looks like ordinary slippage.
steps.result: Executed. $0.04 of value given up, counted against this key's daily budget.

steps.title: Slow bleed, trade 2: the budget runs out
steps.how: The same give-away again. Each one alone is 'fair'; together they leak value.
steps.result: This trade gives up $0.04 against the reference price. Today this key has given up $0.05 of its $0.06 budget.

steps.title: Two refusals later, an ordinary trade waits
steps.how: A normal $1.50 swap from the same key, right after its two refused trades.
steps.result: $1.50 is above this key's $1 autonomy limit, cut from $4 by 2 recent refusals. Waiting for the owner.

steps.title: A hacked guard understates the trade's value
steps.how: The guard claims a 0.3 wNEAR swap is worth $0.05, to stretch the daily cap and the leak budget.
steps.result: Executed at the pool's value: the contract counted $0.37, not the guard's $0.05.
